_schema: Ben's review queue. Canonical store; NEEDS_REVIEW.md is the readable mirror. Entry fields: id, title, raised (ISO date), kind, status, source, what, why_it_matters, options (array, only where there is a genuine fork), recommendation, files, resolution (null until Ben answers).
_note: Companion to backlog.json and review.json, NOT a replacement for either.
PURPOSE: things awaiting BEN'S JUDGEMENT. Three kinds live here:
- 'question'        â€” an open call nobody has made yet, usually surfaced by
doing adjacent work. Not blocking, or it would be a
backlog item with blocked_on set.
- 'decision-taken'  â€” a call made ON BEN'S BEHALF so work could continue.
Recorded here so it can be OVERTURNED rather than
quietly becoming precedent. This is the important half:
an unrecorded delegated decision is indistinguishable
from a decision Ben made.
- 'observation'     â€” something noticed in passing that is too small or too
cross-cutting to file, but which a human should see.
- 'novel-work'      â€” raised by a SESSION about its own task (Ben, 2026-08-20):
the work in hand feels NOVEL â€” no owning authority doc, no
saved role or established pattern fits, or it quietly grows
the project's scope. Raise it AT THE MOMENT the feeling
arises, then continue (or pause, if scope growth is large).
Gives Ben a drift detector: novelty should be chosen, not
accreted.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM review.json: review.json is a BLOCKER list â€” items blocked
on a visual artifact only Ben can produce (a mockup, an annotated screenshot).
Work there cannot proceed at all. Entries here are not blocking; they are
questions and reversible calls. If an entry turns out to need a mockup, move it
to review.json and leave a resolution here pointing at it.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM backlog.json: an entry here is not work. If Ben's answer
creates work, file a backlog item and resolve the entry with that item's id.
LIFECYCLE (revised 2026-08-14, Ben's ruling): this file is TRANSIENT â€” a live
queue of open calls, not a permanent audit trail. Append entries as they arise
and set status to 'resolved' with a resolution once answered, exactly as before.
But do NOT let resolved entries accumulate: prune them promptly rather than
holding them for posterity. The reasoning is not lost â€” it lands in code
comments, an authority doc, or a backlog item's design field at the moment the
work happens, and THAT is the durable record. Ben's own framing: 'the docs
should preserve changes made, and the review queue should only be for things
of that level of importance' â€” i.e. open and unresolved, not a history of
everything ever decided. A large housekeeping sweep this date closed 231
entries down to 2 genuinely open ones on this basis.

ARCHIVAL (2026-08-23): 'prune' now means MOVE, not delete. Run node tools/session/archive_reviews.js to move every resolved entry, verbatim, into docs/development/archive/needs-review-<quarter>.json, then re-render the mirror. The hot file holds open entries only.
SEEDED 2026-08-01 at Ben's request, populated from that session.

PURGE 2026-08-23: 240 open entries -> 18. Every entry referring only to backlog ids <= BL-568 (retired by the same-day backlog purge) was retired; 16 more were answered by reading the current docs and tree. All 223 are frozen verbatim in archive/needs-review-purged-2026-08-23.json, each with a resolution saying why. The survivors are asked as a form: tools/session/register/review_queue.js, built by register/build.js, published at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/53fb4e56-2eae-439e-bcb7-121fa49bd340 . NR-576 records the calls taken in the sweep.

DRAINED 2026-09-01 on Ben's instruction, from 117 open to 0. The queue had become a shadow backlog: most entries named WORK rather than a judgement, so ten backlog items (BL-713..BL-722) were minted to carry it and every entry was closed with a resolution saying where it went. THE RULE THAT KEEPS IT DRAINED, and it is now in CLAUDE.md Rule 0c: a call only Ben can make belongs here; work belongs in backlog.json; a fact worth remembering belongs in the comment or doc next to the code.

items.title: BL-814 carried a phase-6 restructure, and it was deleted with the budget chain
items.source: Re-authoring sprint 35 around generation visibility, on your ruling "drop it - a watched wait needs no budget".
items.what: BL-813, BL-814 and BL-815 were deleted outright under the 2026-08-24 unstarted-plans policy. BL-812 (phase 6 sees roads) was kept, as it is not part of that chain.
items.why_it_matters: BL-814 was filed as a startup-time item but its actual content was a PHASE 6 restructure: retire the warm start so phase 6 becomes the only judge of the position play opens on, and it named a specific known blocker - generate_corporations appends and runs before the registry loads, so phase 6 cannot vary the specialist roster at the live seam. That blocker is a fact about the code, not about the budget, and it will still be true when phase 6 is picked back up. The ruling was about the budget; deleting the restructure with it is my reading of it, not yours.
options: Leave it deleted - the substance is recorded in the sprint 35 risk note and can be re-filed from there.
Re-file the restructure as its own item, under phase 6 rather than under startup time.
items.recommendation: Leave it deleted for now. Phase 6 has no search built at all (BL-770 was cancelled with the board clear), so the restructure has nothing to serve yet; re-file it when phase 6 is next picked up.

items.title: Rounds 4 and 5 break the wizard promise that nothing is generated in it
items.source: Writing the sprint 35 visibility design into STARTUP.md and GENERATION_STRATEGY.md.
items.what: STARTUP.md has said since BL-167 that NOTHING is generated in the wizard - every control move re-runs the chain as a pure throwaway preview and m_world is untouched. Rounds 4 and 5 cannot honour that: the history sim is the most expensive pass in the project. So I wrote them as running the REAL pass inside the round, on a Run press, drawing as it computes - the doc now says the preview model does not transfer.
items.why_it_matters: That promise is not decoration. It is what makes Back a plain revision with no snapshot, and what lets the wizard reroll freely. Rounds that generate for real make Back across round 4 expensive and make a reroll a minute rather than a frame. Your "a watched wait needs no budget" licenses the wait; it does not by itself choose this mechanism over the alternative, which is to collect leans against an illustrative preview and run everything at Begin as today.
options: The pass runs inside the round, on a Run press - the wait is the content (what I wrote).
Leans are collected against an illustrative preview; the real passes still run at Begin behind the loading screen.
items.recommendation: Keep what I wrote. The second option gives the player a lean whose effect they cannot see when they set it, which is the one thing the planetology rounds get right and the reason the wizard works at all.

items.title: A 4000-year pass 1 ending at 1200 CE contradicts prehistory_years = 400 and epoch_year = 0
items.source: Your description of round 4 against the live app: a time-lapse of the first 4000 years, ending at 1200 CE.
items.what: The code defaults are prehistory_years = 400 (hard_coded_world.hpp:73) and epoch_year = 0 CE, with era_band_for_epoch flipping to industrial at 1700. HISTORY.md carries the campaign epoch as 0 CE (your ruling, NR-177), and GENERATION_STRATEGY.md sets the pass 1 / pass 2 boundary at 400 years before the epoch. A 4000-year pass 1 ending at 1200 CE fits none of those three numbers.
items.why_it_matters: It is not a naming mismatch. It reads as a re-basing of the whole calendar: pass 1 becomes 2800 BCE to 1200 CE, pass 2 runs 1200 CE to an epoch that must now be well past 1700 - which puts the campaign in the industrial band rather than the ancient one, and that band choice reaches into eras, resources and the military roster. It also multiplies the most expensive pass in the project by ten, against your other requirement for this round, which is that it be rapid.
options: The epoch moves late (a modern arc) and 1200 CE is the pass 1 / pass 2 boundary year. Pass 1 is 4000 years, pass 2 is 1200 to the epoch.
The epoch stays at 0 CE and 1200 CE is wrong - the time-lapse ends at the epoch, whatever it is.
4000 years is the SPAN and 1200 CE is illustrative; the real numbers fall out of the cost measurement.
items.recommendation: Option 1, because it is what you actually described and the arc you named - through to a stable dark age - is a medieval end point, not a classical one. But it moves the campaign into the industrial era band, so it is not a small consequence and I am not taking it on your behalf.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-09-08 by Ben the same day: "another focused pass on economy from 1560 to 1960". That is option 1 - the epoch moves late. The calendar is now stated rather than derived: 4000 years to 1200 CE, a coast to 1560, then 1560-1960, epoch 1960. Written into GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Pass 2 is the economy pass and lore/HISTORY.md § The epoch and the run. The consequence I flagged holds and is now carried by BL-831: an epoch of 1960 puts the campaign in the INDUSTRIAL era band, not the ancient one, and that owes a deliberate digest re-bless.

items.title: The 1200 - 1560 gap is unsimulated, and I have written it up as a deliberate coast
items.source: Your two spans: pass 1 ends at 1200 CE, pass 2 runs 1560 to 1960.
items.what: That leaves 360 years nothing steps. I have written it into GENERATION_STRATEGY.md and HISTORY.md as a deliberate COAST rather than a gap: pass 1 ends in a stable dark age, a span defined by little changing is not worth simulating, and the world arrives at 1560 holding what 1200 left it.
items.why_it_matters: It reads as intentional and it fits the arc you named - a stable dark age is precisely a span where skipping loses little. But you did not say it, I inferred it, and the alternative reading is that pass 1 should run to 1560 and 1200 was approximate. The two differ by 360 years of assimilation and grudge decay, which are the accumulators that move on their own even when borders do not.
options: A deliberate coast, with self-moving accumulators advanced cheaply across it (what I wrote).
Pass 1 runs to 1560 and the two spans meet.
1200 was approximate; the boundary is wherever the measurement says it can afford to be.
items.recommendation: Keep the coast. It is the cheapest span in the whole calendar and the one where the least is lost - but BL-831 has to name which accumulators cross it, because silently dropping 360 years of assimilation would undo the lever that makes conquest fragile.

items.title: The wizard has no entries in the action dictionary, and the five rounds did not add any
items.source: Merging the wizard shell (BL-816, BL-824) and verifying it live.
items.what: CLAUDE.md says any control change updates its ACTIONS.json entry. The wizard gained two rounds, a per-round Reroll, and a Begin that moved. None of it was recorded, because ACTIONS.json has no startup family at all - its dictionary is gameplay.* and canvas.* only.
items.why_it_matters: Either the pre-game wizard is deliberately outside the action dictionary - defensible, since the dictionary exists for an agent playing the game and nobody plays the wizard - or it is a gap that has been quietly widening since the wizard was built. The rule as written does not distinguish, so every session touching startup will face this again and answer it differently.
options: The wizard is out of scope for ACTIONS.json; say so in the doc so it stops being a question.
Add a startup.* family and backfill the wizard.
items.recommendation: Out of scope, stated explicitly. The dictionary is the AI seam and no agent presses Begin; a startup family would be inventory nobody reads. But it needs writing down, because silence is what made this a question.
